cap01.title: Every role in the school, not only teachers.
cap01.lede: An org chart per year, a catalog of 232 roles—teachers, leadership, education assistants, special needs (PIE), administration, board and school owner—with aliases, EN and ES-CL names and gender variants, and an AI-assisted match that proposes the right template for each role in the school.

orgChart.body: A tree of roles per year, with Current and Proposed (catalog) views. Each node shows the role, its code and the person holding it; the editor reviews the hierarchy and detects orphan roles.

catalog.title: A catalog of 232 roles

cap02.title: From 600 questions to the Principal's rubric.
cap02.lede: Every question in the bank declares its area, its dimension, which 360° perspectives can answer it, its priority and weight, and the regulation behind it. Eleva selects the ones that apply to the role—116 for Principal, grouped in 2 frameworks and 11 dimensions—and assembles the rubric. You review it, expand it or collapse it.

cap03.title: Four perspectives, six stages, weights you define.
cap03.lede: The school defines how much each 360° perspective weighs and which stages each evaluation process goes through. The school owner sets the central configuration; each school can override it.

weights.title: How much does each perspective weigh?
weights.body: Upward (the team evaluates its manager), Self-assessment, Manager (the manager evaluates the team) and Peer to Peer. The weights define the final calculation and must add up to exactly 100.

rows.name: Self-assessment
rows.hint: each person evaluates their own performance

weights.note: Must add up to exactly 100 · Simulate missing types

plate.caption: Perspective weights · example 25 / 25 / 25 / 25 · Total 100 / 100
plate.alt: Eleva wizard step ¿Cuánto pesa cada perspectiva?: Upward, Self-assessment, Manager and Peer to Peer at 25 % each, a ring chart at 100 % and Total 100 / 100.

stages.title: Six stages, central configuration
stages.body: The school owner defines the default stages per perspective type; each school can override them on its own stages page.

items.name: In Feedback
items.desc: The evaluator sends the evaluation to the evaluee for feedback

items.name: Finalized
items.desc: Evaluation finalized; its results count in the reports

items.name: Closed
items.desc: Definitive closure; only an administrator can reopen it

stages.alwaysNote: Some stages are always active; the rest are switched on or off per school.
stages.note: Changes apply to new processes: each process freezes its flow when generated, so historical processes keep the configuration they were created with.

plate.caption: Default stages per perspective · Central configuration
plate.alt: Central stage configuration in Eleva: six stages from 0 to 5, In Preparation, Started, In Feedback, Feedback Answered, Finalized and Closed, some always active and others switchable.

cap04.title: Achievement per domain and improvement suggestions, ready for reports.
cap04.lede: Each evaluator answers the rubric on a Likert 1–5 scale. Eleva calculates achievement per domain according to its weighting, shows progress (32 of 32 answered · 100 %) and delivers one improvement suggestion per domain. When an evaluation becomes Finalized, its results count in the reports.

normativa.lede: The questions selected for each role are aligned with national regulation and professional frameworks: Ley Karin, Teaching Career, MBDLE, Personal Data Protection, School Climate and more. Every question in the rubric shows the laws behind it, for consistent, defensible evaluations.

faq.title: Notes.
faq.lede: Six frequently asked questions, answered with what the product does.

items.a: No: 232 roles, including leadership, education assistants, special needs (PIE), administrative staff, board and school owner, with correct names, aliases and gender variants.

items.q: Where do the questions come from?
items.a: From a curated bank of 600 questions in 13 collections and 24 areas. Each one declares dimension, 360° perspectives, priority, weight and the regulation behind it.
It proposes: role templates with a confidence percentage and an explanation, the rubric per role and improvement suggestions per domain. A person always has the last word.
Four perspectives—Upward, Self-assessment, Manager and Peer to Peer—with weights that must add up to 100; answers on a Likert 1–5 scale and achievement per domain.

items.q: Does it work for several schools?
items.a: Yes. The school owner defines a central configuration with default stages per perspective type; each school can override it, and each process freezes its flow when generated.
Role-based access, audit log and CSV / PDF export. SSO / SAML available and MFA supported.
